character_sheet: The T-Rex is a hostile tyrannosaur: a long torso and hips with five back spines, a neck to a head with a snout, a hinged jaw and two head spikes, two tiny arms, two hip spikes, a tail with an extension, and two four-piece legs (ModelTRex.createBodyLayer, ModelTRex.java:80-219 — the parts carry the modeller's opaque names, shape1 to shape21, mapped to anatomy in the glossary). It has 160 HP, 22 attack and 14 armour (MobStats.TREX, createAttributes TRex.java:249-257; a 200 constant for its own health checks, :272-274), fights on the dinosaur melee goal — a bite within four blocks plus half the target's width on two dice, a chase at 1.25, prey found in a 20-block box (DinosaurMeleeAttackGoal.Presets.trex, TRex.java:76-77) — with a 1.2 knockback (doHurtTarget :314-328), re-picks its target every fifth tick and avenges hits (selectTarget :124-131, RevengeGoal :186), and wanders and looks about between (:78-80). Cactus cannot hurt it (hurt :331-345). It spawns at night in the dark above y 50 under a clear air column with no other T-Rex within 24 blocks (checkSpawnRules :356-365) in the Chaos and Mining biomes (chaos_biome.json, mining_biome.json). Read it as a heavy two-legged stalker: a swinging stride, a snapping jaw, the little arms twitching.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.2 of the rig (TRexRenderer.java:28, applied :40; shadow 1.0 x 1.2) on a 128x128 sheet (ModelTRex.java:219); 2.0 x 4.2 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:168-169). The design's row says: rename nothing — the opaque shape names are final; this glossary maps them to anatomy.

labels.shape1: torso (the 10x18x31 body block; static; intended hitbox part 'shape1')
labels.shape3: tail (the 7x7x25 tail block; static; intended hitbox part 'shape3')

labels.rightleg: right thigh (opposite the left; intended hitbox part 'rightleg')

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed above a 0.1 threshold (zero below it): every piece of a leg swings together about its rest (thigh −0.174, shin 0.506, ankle −0.401, foot 0), the right leg +a and the left −a
groups.plain: the two legs stride with the walking speed, each leg swinging as one stiff four-piece chain, the left opposite the right
groups.math: a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 1.3) * pi * 0.25 * amount : 0; rightleg.xRot = -0.174 + a, rightleg2.xRot = 0.506 + a, rightleg3.xRot = -0.401 + a, rightleg4.xRot = a; leftleg.xRot = -0.174 - a, leftleg2.xRot = 0.506 - a, leftleg3.xRot = -0.401 - a, leftleg4.xRot = -a
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 (ANIM_SPEED 1.0): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.3 = 4.83 ticks

groups.name: jaw
groups.amplitude: attacking: pi x 0.18 = 0.565 rad (32 deg) about 0.52; not attacking: still at 0.1
groups.plain: the jaw chomps while the attacking flag is set and hangs nearly shut otherwise
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (TRex.java:33, set by the melee goal's IntConsumer at :76) selects; note the phase is ageInTicks x 0.45 without the ANIM_SPEED factor
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.45: the natural period is 13.96 ticks

groups.name: arms
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.05 = 0.157 rad (9 deg) about −0.523, both arms together, at all times
groups.plain: the two tiny arms wave slowly up and down together whatever the creature does
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.1: the natural period is 62.8 ticks

behaviour: One speed-scaled stride at 1.3 rad/tick (a 4.8-tick period) above a walking-speed threshold of 0.1: the two legs swing 45 degrees at top speed as stiff four-piece chains, the left opposite the right (ModelTRex.java:224-236). Standing still the legs rest.

The jaw chomps 32 degrees at 0.45 rad/tick about 0.52 while the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte is set (TRex.java:33; the melee goal at :76 sets it within reach) and hangs at 0.1 otherwise (:238-240). The two tiny arms wave 9 degrees at 0.1 rad/tick at all times (:242-243).
The torso, hips, tail and its extension, neck, head, snout, the head and hip spikes and the five back spines are static; the head does not track the look, and the walk position plays no part.
The bite is the melee goal's (DinosaurMeleeAttackGoal, TRex.java:76-77; doHurtTarget :314-328) — nothing in the code fires an animation for it.

in `attack`'s wind-up: the jaw chomp (:239) with the head lowered and turned on the target — the code never turns the head; the contract's aggro_idle carries it — offered now (TEST-011 (b): the flag's writes traced into the goal, from the setter handed at TRex.java:76)

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelTRex row (geckolib_migration_design.md:458): 'shape5 [1.3,1.1] @1 (head), shape1 [2,2.5] @0.5 (torso), left/right upper/lower legs [0.7,1.8] @0.5, shape3 [1.2,1.2] @0.25 (tail), tail_extension [0.7,0.8] @0.25'. shape5, shape1, shape3 and tail_extension resolve as written (ModelTRex.createBodyLayer; the field names at ModelTRex.java:55-77 confirm shape5 = head, shape1 = torso, shape3 = tail). 'left/right upper/lower legs' is not a bone name: taken as the thigh and shin of each leg — leftleg / leftleg2 and rightleg / rightleg2 (the ankle leftleg3 / rightleg3 and the foot leftleg4 / rightleg4 stay visual). The row: 'Rename nothing in conversion'.
formulas: `ModelTRex.poseFrom` (ModelTRex.java:231-252; orig ModelTRex.java:216-254 in `render` (func_78088_a, :211-255; func_78087_a at :263-265 is a bare super call); the original's wingspeed 0.2 from `new ModelTRex(0.2f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:417 is not the port's, whose ANIM_SPEED is 1.0 - the hooks' landing recorded the departure): while the walking speed is above a tenth the swing is the cosine of the age in ticks times 1.3, times pi, times 0.25, times the walking speed, else 0; the four right leg pieces pitch -0.174, 0.506, -0.401 and 0 plus it, the four left pieces the same rests minus it. Attacking, the jaw pitches 0.52 plus the cosine of the age times 0.45, times pi, times 0.18; else 0.1. The two arms (the rig's shape17 and shape11) pitch -0.523 plus the cosine of the age times 0.1, times pi, times 0.05. The walk position and the head angles play no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (TRexGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
